external_entities.name: duty engineer
external_entities.description: A duty engineer who opens the dispatch console in a browser.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network. They open the dispatch console in their browser.

external_entities.name: scheduling partner
external_entities.description: Another company that publishes tomorrow's planned work through a SOAP feed.
external_entities.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company, publishes tomorrow's planned work.

processes.name: dispatch console
processes.description: A single-page JavaScript application used by duty engineers.
processes.source_excerpt: The console is a single-page JavaScript app
processes.notes: Nobody wrote down how an engineer signs in to it. The API's allowed CORS origins and credential setting are also undocumented.

processes.name: corporate web host
processes.description: The corporate web host that serves the dispatch console.
processes.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

processes.name: dispatch API
processes.description: The API called by the dispatch console and schedule importer, running in the production control plane.
processes.source_excerpt: The dispatch API runs in the production control plane.
processes.notes: The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

processes.name: schedule importer
processes.description: An hourly importer that pulls the partner's SOAP feed, parses XML, archives downloaded documents, and posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API.
processes.source_excerpt: Our schedule importer runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The importer presents an API token that was issued when it was built and has not been rotated.

data_stores.name: dispatch database
data_stores.description: A database containing job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.
data_stores.source_excerpt: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.
data_stores.notes: How the database is protected at rest is not written down anywhere.

data_stores.name: schedule archive
data_stores.description: A folder on the corporate file store where each downloaded scheduling document is written.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive, a folder on the corporate file store.

data_flows.name: open console
data_flows.description: A duty engineer opens the dispatch console in a browser.
data_flows.source_excerpt: They open the dispatch console in their browser.

data_flows.name: serve console
data_flows.description: The corporate web host serves the single-page JavaScript dispatch console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: our corporate web host serves it

data_flows.name: call API
data_flows.description: The dispatch console calls the dispatch API cross-origin.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console calls the dispatch API.
data_flows.notes: The console and API are served from different origins. The API's allowed origins and whether it allows credentials are undocumented.

data_flows.name: live job status
data_flows.description: The dispatch console opens and holds a WebSocket to the dispatch API for live job status.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The console also opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API and holds it open for live job status.
data_flows.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the socket runs over TLS, whether its handshake is authenticated, or whether it checks the engineer's session again after it is open.

data_flows.name: read and write
data_flows.description: The dispatch API reads and writes dispatch data in the dispatch database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
data_flows.data_description: job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and creating token or session

data_flows.name: pull SOAP feed
data_flows.description: The schedule importer pulls the partner's planned-work feed every hour.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every hour it pulls the partner's SOAP feed over HTTPS
data_flows.notes: Nothing was written down about how the partner identifies the importer or how the importer identifies the partner.
data_flows.data_description: tomorrow's planned work in an XML document

data_flows.name: write documents
data_flows.description: The schedule importer writes each downloaded document into the schedule archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive

data_flows.name: post work orders
data_flows.description: The schedule importer posts parsed work orders to the dispatch API using an API token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The importer then posts the parsed work orders to the same dispatch API the console calls. It presents an API token.
data_flows.notes: The API token was issued when the importer was built and nobody has rotated it since.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where duty engineers and the schedule importer are located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Duty engineers sit on the corporate network.
trust_boundaries.notes: The schedule importer is also stated to run on this network.

trust_boundaries.name: production control plane
trust_boundaries.description: The same-company zone holding the live estate, with authority to move a crew and change the work a depot does that day.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The control plane is the same company and the same staff, but it is the zone that holds the live estate
trust_boundaries.notes: A corporate laptop holds none of the control-plane rights. The control plane is not reachable from the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: scheduling partner
trust_boundaries.description: The zone controlled by the other company that publishes the planned-work feed.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: A scheduling partner, which is another company

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch database is confidential because it contains crew mobile numbers, job orders, and token or session data.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the database holds job orders, crew names, crew mobile numbers, and the token or session that created each job order.

assumptions.assumption: The dispatch API presents a web interface because it is accessed cross-origin by the console and supports a WebSocket endpoint.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the API answers the console cross-origin and that the console opens a WebSocket to the dispatch API.
